title.suggested: The Last Goss Fight and Allen's Flight to England

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic recalled Tom Allen's September 1876 fight with Joe Goss in Kentucky, given to Goss on an alleged foul, after which Allen fled through Canada to England while Goss was jailed.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Sunday Morning, March 31, 1895, page 40.

facts.fact: Allen beat Ben Hogan in three rounds in November; Hogan's friends rushed into the ring and pointed pistols at him
facts.quote: and in November of the same year I got away with Ben Hogan in three rounds. Hogan's friends rushed into the ring with their pistols and pointed them at me, but I was not hurt and got the fight.

facts.fact: Allen's fight with Joe Goss in Kentucky in September 1876 was given to Goss on an alleged foul by referee 'Eph' Holland of New York, chosen against the wishes of the Allen side
Goss was arrested and jailed for a year and a half in Kentucky for the 1876 fight
After the Goss fight Allen escaped through Canada and took a steamer to England, staying away a long time
Allen was about $25,000 ahead when he left, and lost most of it making a book through England
Allen's last fight in England before coming to America in 1869 was a draw with Joe Goss after 34 rounds for the middleweight championship
On his return to England Allen beat Tompkin Gilbert in sixteen minutes for £100 and the championship of England

notes: The article dates Allen's arrival in America to 1869, unlike fact 006 (July 1867). The year of the Hogan fight is in the preceding text, outside this clipping. '100 pounds' for the Gilbert stakes is read as pounds sterling.
